title: Keyboard shortcuts in English keyboard layout for any language
summary: A Russian keyboard layout changes the displayed English shortcut key letter in PowerToys Settings; the reported version is 0.63.0.

judgment.rationale: The reported layout-dependent key glyph is specific, but it was last confirmed on 0.63.0 and current Settings formatting has not been tied to the inspected Keyboard Manager code.
evidence: Issue #21268 reports the key glyph changing from T to Cyrillic Е when Russian is active.
Current main Keyboard Manager layout-map formatting is adjacent evidence, not proof of the Settings menu implementation.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm the same label on current stable under English and Russian layouts before changing Settings formatting.

fix_assessment.rationale: A layout-independent label is a plausible fix only if the behavior still reproduces in current Settings.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Settings shortcut labels stable across input layouts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Settings menu may be rendering a key label from the active input layout, but the current issue evidence does not establish the responsible Settings code path.
plan: Confirm the behavior on a current build and trace the Settings menu shortcut-label formatter.
Separate the stable displayed key name from active-layout character translation without changing the configured shortcut.
Add focused coverage that compares the same menu label under English and Russian input layouts.
verification: Verify the same shortcut label remains stable under both layouts while the shortcut still invokes the same command.

confidence.rationale: The old report is clear, but current Settings behavior and formatter ownership are unverified.

issue_context.summary: A Russian keyboard layout changes the displayed English shortcut key letter in PowerToys Settings; the reported version is 0.63.0.
known_information: The reporter says the same Settings menu item shows Win+Shift+T with English active but Win+Shift+Е with Russian active.
The report is from PowerToys 0.63.0 and the latest issue discussion is from 2022.
inferences: If this still reproduces, Settings may be displaying the active-layout character rather than a stable key label; the report does not establish which Settings formatter is responsible.
issue_context.analysis: The reproduction is specific, but it is old and the inspected current Keyboard Manager formatter is not proof of the separate Settings menu-label path. Confirm current behavior before choosing a formatter change.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and two comments; there is no newer reporter confirmation or linked fixing PR in its discussion.

Current main at 6b3db15615e3e549b89790e0bd83c82d262c22e0 has Keyboard Manager human-readable shortcut formatting through LayoutMap.GetKeyName in trace.cpp; this does not establish the Settings menu path. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/6b3db15615e3e549b89790e0bd83c82d262c22e0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/trace.cpp#L160-L166

information_gaps.information: Whether one Settings menu shortcut still changes from a Latin key name to a Cyrillic character when switching the active input layout on current PowerToys
information_gaps.why_needed: The report predates current builds and the inspected Keyboard Manager formatter does not prove that the Settings shortcut label uses the same path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the current stable build, compare the same Settings menu item with English and Russian layouts active; include the PowerToys version and a screenshot of only that item, with personal content hidden.

actions.label: Approve Keep Settings shortcut labels stable across input layouts
Confirm shortcut label across English and Russian layouts

comment.body: Thanks for the clear example: the same Settings shortcut shows `Win+Shift+T` with English active and `Win+Shift+Е` with Russian active. Since the report is from PowerToys 0.63.0, could you confirm whether this still happens on the current stable build? Please include the PowerToys version and a screenshot of that one menu item with each layout active (hide personal information). This will show whether the Settings label still follows the input layout before we change its formatter.
